classification.difficultyReason: Same task as the reference parts: divide a quartic with unknown m and n by a quadratic, read off the remainder, and set both coefficients to zero. Routine linked procedure, about 38.

content.prompt: If $x^4+x^3-8x^2+mx+n$ is exactly divisible by $x^2-2x+3$, find $m$ and $n$.

answer.short: $m=19$, $n=-15$. Long division gives remainder $(m-19)x+(n+15)$; exact divisibility requires both coefficients to be zero.
answer.worked:
The successive quotient terms in long division are $x^2$, $3x$ and $-5$.
$$\begin{aligned}
(x^4+x^3-8x^2+mx+n)-x^2(x^2-2x+3)&=3x^3-11x^2+mx+n\\
(3x^3-11x^2+mx+n)-3x(x^2-2x+3)&=-5x^2+(m-9)x+n\\
(-5x^2+(m-9)x+n)-(-5)(x^2-2x+3)&=(m-19)x+(n+15).
\end{aligned}$$
Thus
$$\begin{aligned}
x^4+x^3-8x^2+mx+n&=(x^2-2x+3)(x^2+3x-5)+(m-19)x+(n+15).
\end{aligned}$$
Exact divisibility means the remainder is zero, so
$$\begin{aligned}
m-19&=0\\
n+15&=0\\
m&=19,\qquad n=-15.
\end{aligned}$$
